title: ControlNet strength, start and end percent

questions.q: On an SD 1.x model, what does end_percent 0.5 set?
options: Half of your steps run with the control
A noise level, the sigma at timestep about 500, below which the control is off
The control strength falls by half
The last half of the steps run with the control
questions.answer: A noise level, the sigma at timestep about 500, below which the control is off
questions.why: percent_to_sigma turns it into a noise level. Each step compares its own sigma with that level. Your step count is not part of it.

questions.q: In the lab, end_percent 0.5 with 20 steps gives how many steps on with exponential?
questions.why: The exponential schedule spends more steps at low noise, under the end level. normal gives 10 and karras 9.

questions.q: You run img2img at denoise 0.5 with start 0 and end 0.5, normal scheduler. What happens?
options: The control runs on no step, with no warning
questions.answer: The control runs on no step, with no warning
questions.why: The run starts at sigma 1.548, already under the end level 1.616, so every step is outside the window.

questions.q: You chain two ControlNets, each at strength 1.0. What does the U-Net get?
options: The first one's, with the second as a fallback
questions.why: control_merge adds the earlier ControlNet's residuals to its own, each scaled by its own strength.

questions.q: You set start_percent 0.8 and end_percent 0.2. What happens?
questions.why: The level for 0.8 is below the level for 0.2, so every sigma is above one or below the other. The lab counts 0 steps.
